report.summary: Saturation, not errors: around 21:21:18 the event loop pinned at full utilisation with p99 delay up ~30x, while the 10-connection DB pool filled to its ceiling and requests queued, pushing pool wait p95 above a second. HTTP p95 latency, stable near 0.010 s all window, breached the 1 s SLO by detection. Warn-level \"order rejected\" logs are unchanged from baseline across both versions and no error pattern appeared. Most probable cause: in-process blocking work starving connection release and exhausting the pool; a slow DB dependency is the leading unverified candidate.

timeline.event: Pre-incident baseline: p95 latency {lat_base_max}, pool used {pool_used_first}, pending {pend_first}, event-loop utilisation {el_util_min}.
Onset: event-loop utilisation hits {el_util_max}, p99 delay rises to {el_delay_max}, pool used jumps to {pool_used_max} of {pool_max}; pending waiters climb toward {pend_max}.
p95 latency first deviates from baseline, rising from {lat_first}.
Pool pending requests peak at {pend_max}; pool wait p95 reaches {wait_max}.
Last "order rejected" warn line in the incident window; {warn_inc_count} such lines versus {warn_base_count} in baseline.
p95 latency peaks at {lat_max}, breaching the 1 s SLO threshold; event-loop delay p99 also peaks at {el_delay_max}.

hypotheses.statement: DB connection pool exhaustion (all {pool_max} connections held with requests queuing, wait p95 at {wait_max}) caused the p95 latency to rise to {lat_max}, because server-side work stalls while holding connections and prevents release.

In-process CPU-bound work saturating the single-threaded event loop (utilisation at {el_util_max}, p99 delay {el_delay_max}) caused the incident by blocking request handling and starving pool connection release.

A slowdown in the downstream database dependency (queries blocking the event loop) caused the incident, showing up as event-loop utilisation {el_util_max} and pool wait p95 {wait_max} while latency reached {lat_max}.

observations.statement: HTTP p95 latency was flat at ~0.0097 s throughout the baseline window immediately before the incident.
In the incident window p95 latency rose from {lat_first} to {lat_max}, peaking at 21:21:48.502Z.
Event-loop utilisation jumped from a baseline-like {el_util_min} to {el_util_max}, pegged at the ceiling for the last three samples from 21:21:18.502Z onward.
Event-loop p99 delay rose from {el_delay_min} to {el_delay_max} across the same onset samples.
Pool used connections went from {pool_used_first} to {pool_used_max}, exactly saturating the constant pool limit of {pool_max} connections.
Pending pool requests went from {pend_first} to {pend_max} at 21:21:33.502Z, still {pend_last} waiters at the end of the window.
Pool wait p95 rose from {wait_first} to {wait_max}, reaching over a second of queueing per request.
Loki shows the same single warn pattern "order rejected" in the incident window ({warn_inc_count} lines) as in the preceding baseline window ({warn_base_count} lines), with no error-severity pattern.
The warn pattern appears under both service versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 during the incident window, while baseline carries only 1.0.0.
Overall log volume stayed near {info_max} info lines per minute and never exceeded {warn_max} warn lines per minute, so there was no log-volume surge accompanying the latency spike.

recommendations.action: Query db_operation_p95 (and DB-side query latency) for the onset window against the pre-incident baseline to determine whether a slow query is what blocks the event loop.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_3 is the leading unverified candidate and hyp_1/hyp_2 cannot be separated without downstream latency data; metric budget ran out before this query.

recommendations.action: Profile or sample the event loop during a reproduction to identify the blocking code path and confirm whether it is CPU-bound work or awaited I/O.
recommendations.rationale: Distinguishes hyp_2 (in-process CPU-bound work saturating the loop) from hyp_3 (slow dependency).

recommendations.action: Instrument pool acquire/release timing and add a per-request pool-hold duration metric so held connections can be attributed to specific endpoints.
recommendations.rationale: Confirms whether connections are held by stalled handlers, as hyp_1 asserts, and identifies which call path to fix.

recommendations.action: Check request rate and concurrency at 21:21:18 to determine whether the pool saturation was driven by a traffic spike rather than by slow work holding connections.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1 assumes saturation from stalling work; a traffic surge would change the mitigation (rate limiting or pool sizing rather than code fix).
